h: לְרֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ מְנַחֵם אָב, ב׳ Rosh Chodesh Menachem Av, 2

p: מוּסְפֵי שַׁבָּת קוֹדֶם לְמוּסְפֵי רֹאשׁ חוֹדֶשׁ
the Mussafin of Shabbos precede the Mussafin of Rosh Chodesh.
are more sanctified than those of Shabbos,
since it is called a mo'ed.
why the Mussafin of Rosh Chodesh are called,
on the grounds that it is called a mo'ed,
more sanctified than those of Shabbos,
of which it is explicitly written (Bereishis 2:3):
But the matter of the qualities
and which of them takes precedence,
And likewise the quality of holiness too
is what is from man's side.
is a holiness that is fixed and established
since the six days of Creation,
from the side of Hashem Yisbarach,
which is not so with Rosh Chodesh,
for it is not found at all in the Torah
it is only from the side of Yisrael,
רַשִׁ״י שְׁמוֹת יב, ב מֵרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה כ, א)
the head of the beis din says "Mekudash,"
and all the people answer after him,
only from the side of Yisrael.
הַקְּדוּשָּׁה הוּא מִצַּד ה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ גַּם כֵּן
the holiness is from the side of Hashem Yisbarach as well,
for "mikra kodesh" is written of them,
for it is Yisrael who fix them,
as they said in the Gemara (Pesachim ibid.);
which is not so with Rosh Chodesh,
whose holiness is not found at all
and it is only from the side of Yisrael;
and this is called "sanctified" from the side of Yisrael.
And we find in the Gemara (Bava Metzia 38a):
"A person prefers one kav of his own
to nine kabin of his fellow's."
And according to what it concludes there,
when everywhere one takes for hyperbole
up to the attribute of Malchus
are holy from the side of Hashem Yisbarach;
is only from the side of Yisrael.
And this is the matter of Shabbos,
whose holiness is from the side of Hashem Yisbarach—
all of which flow into Knesses Yisrael,
"To know that I am Hashem Who sanctifies you."
whose holiness is only from the side of Yisrael—
that is, the holiness from man's side,
more than nine kabin of his fellow's,
which are from the side of Hashem Yisbarach.
And "his fellow" is the Holy One, blessed be He,
do not do to your fellow"—
this is the Holy One, blessed be He, etc.
And this is why the Gemara called
as against the Mussafin of Shabbos:
for this is the essence of holiness,
which is only from the side of Yisrael,
and it is called "his own kav."
And this is the matter we find:
in one verse it is written (Yechezkel 46:1),
"And on the day of Shabbos it shall be opened,
and on the day of the new moon it shall be opened"—
placing Shabbos before the new moon;
"And it shall be, from new moon to new moon
placing the new moon before Shabbos.
But from the side of Hashem Yisbarach,
the holiness of Shabbos comes first;
and here, where it is written,
"all flesh shall come to bow down,"
therefore it placed the new moon before Shabbos,
for the reason that a person prefers his own kav
גַּבֵּי שׁוּנַמִּית כְּתִיב (מְלָכִים ב ד, כג)
regarding the Shunamis it is written (Melachim II 4:23),
"It is neither new moon nor Shabbos":
since it speaks of greeting one's Rebbi,
it placed the new moon before Shabbos,
מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאָדָם רוֹצֶה בְּקַב שֶׁלּוֹ וְכוּלֵּי
because a person prefers his own kav, etc.
The main source where we find
concerning Rosh Chodesh that it is called a mo'ed
is learned only from the month of Av,
'He proclaimed a mo'ed against me,' etc."
וְהוּא דִּבְחוֹדֶשׁ זֶה כְּתִיב (הוֹשֵׁעַ ב, יג)
This is because concerning this month it is written (Hoshea 2:13):
"And I will put an end to all her joy,
her festival, her new moon, and her Shabbos";
Hashem has caused festival and Shabbos to be forgotten in Tziyon."
And in this month the Sages perceived
דִּבְרֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ יֵשׁ גַּם כֵּן קְדוּשָּׁה
that on Rosh Chodesh too there is holiness,
and it is called a mo'ed.
This is in the manner of what is said
in the name of the Rebbe, Reb Ber, zt"l,
"All her pursuers overtook her between the straits"—
that is, all who pursue Hashem,
who pursue the attainment of Hashem Yisbarach,
Him Who spoke and the world came to be,
in these days, which are called Bein HaMetzarim.
And he gave a parable for this:
when the king is in his palace,
it is hard to come into his chamber,
but when he is on the road,
it is easier to come to him.
did the Sages perceive more strongly
the holiness of the month, which is from the side of Yisrael—
that Rosh Chodesh is called a mo'ed—
and from it they learned for every Rosh Chodesh
(as was explained in the previous maamar).
And in the Gemara (Zevachim ibid.) it concludes:
is effective for its own Mussafin,
but not effective for the Mussafin of Shabbos?"
That is, when Rosh Chodesh falls on Shabbos,
so that the holiness of Shabbos too
will be counted as "his own kav."
דְּבֶאֱמֶת גַּם בְּשַׁבָּת כְּתִיב (שְׁמוֹת כ, ח)
For in truth regarding Shabbos too it is written (Shemos 20:8):
"Remember the day of Shabbos to sanctify it,"
that Yisrael must bring holiness into Shabbos.
And Shabbos is called "the first of the holy convocations"
do Yisrael have the ability to bring holiness
into Rosh Chodesh and the festivals?
הוּא רַק עַל יְדֵי שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל קְדוֹשִׁים
It is only because Yisrael are holy,
when it is filled from what is holy, becomes sanctified,
וְהַיְינוּ עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (שַׁבָּת י, ב)
That is, according to what they said (Shabbos 10b):
מַתָּנָה טוֹבָה יֵשׁ לִי בְּבֵית גְּנָזַי
I have a good gift in My treasure house,
and I wish to give it to Yisrael," etc.
And through the power of this holiness—
"that I am Hashem Who sanctifies you"—
that the Jew bring holiness into it,
But the essence of the holiness of Shabbos
is from the side of Hashem Yisbarach.
But when Rosh Chodesh falls on Shabbos,
also for the added holiness of Shabbos,
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה נִקְרָא גַּם כֵּן עַל שֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל
so that it too will be called by the name of Yisrael,
who accept the yoke of His kingship, may His Name be blessed.
